claims.text: Overall wear resistance during high-temperature sliding is governed by coating grain size and grain-boundary density.
Microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding is governed by coating grain size and grain-boundary density.
Changing grain size changes grain-boundary density.
Grain-boundary density influences dislocation diffusion and migration.
Grain refinement can be produced by optimizing deposition parameters or applying post-deposition heat treatment.
The intended high-temperature sliding regime is above 500°C.
Grain refinement increases wear resistance relative to the baseline-grain-size coating.
Grain refinement reduces microscopic deformation relative to the baseline-grain-size coating.
Refinement below 100 nm may decrease wear resistance.
The possible decrease in wear resistance below 100 nm is caused by increased susceptibility to grain-boundary sliding.
The grain-size–wear-resistance relationship may depend on substrate material and operating conditions.

contradictions.description: The general prediction says grain refinement increases wear resistance, whereas the boundary states that refinement below 100 nm may decrease wear resistance. The general prediction is not explicitly restricted to grain sizes at or above 100 nm.

Decreased wear resistance after refinement is defined as falsifying the hypothesis, but it is also predicted as a possible outcome below 100 nm due to grain-boundary sliding. Thus, an outcome allowed by the stated boundary could incorrectly be treated as falsification.
